title: NB Telephone Headquarters, Main Street since 1933
description: The Farmers Telephone Company began in 1905 in Windsor, Carleton County, to provide local farmers with telephone service. The first line linked ten phones from Windsor to Hartland. In 1907, NB Telephone and Central Telephone Company merged, but Farmers Telephone did not join because of high fees. Instead, they expanded quickly, opening exchanges in Hartland, East Florenceville, and Woodstock, to connect them. George O. Britton managed the company, which had about 800 customers by 1919. In 1921, NB Telephone Company bought Farmers Telephone, and George Britton stayed as manager until 1933. The photo shows the new NB Telephone Company office, across from the old Farmers Exchange office, in the Anna Martin building, which is still present today on the east side of Upper Main.
